questions.question: What occurs when an uncharged metal sphere is brought near a positively charged rod without touching it?
options: Negative charges accumulate on the near side and positive charges on the far side due to electrostatic induction
The sphere acquires an overall permanent positive charge immediately
Electrons leap out into the surrounding air from the sphere
The sphere turns into an electromagnet
questions.correct_answer: Negative charges accumulate on the near side and positive charges on the far side due to electrostatic induction
questions.explanation: The positive rod attracts free conduction electrons toward the near surface of the sphere, leaving an equal deficit of electrons (positive charge) on the opposite side.

questions.question: Why does a piece of paper get attracted to a comb that has been run through dry hair?
options: The charged comb induces opposite charges on the nearest surface of the neutral paper, resulting in net electrostatic attraction
Friction between air molecules glues the paper to the comb
The paper becomes magnetized by the plastic comb
Air pressure pushes the paper toward the vacuum created by the comb
questions.correct_answer: The charged comb induces opposite charges on the nearest surface of the neutral paper, resulting in net electrostatic attraction
questions.explanation: Although the paper is overall neutral, the comb's electric field polarizes molecules in the paper, bringing opposite induced charges closer than like charges and creating net attraction.

questions.question: How does doubling the cross-sectional area of a wire affect its electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistance is inversely proportional to cross-sectional area: R = ρL/A. Doubling area A cuts resistance R by a factor of 2.

questions.question: How does doubling the length of a wire affect its electrical resistance?
options: The resistance decreases by a factor of 4
questions.explanation: From R = ρL/A, resistance is directly proportional to wire length L. Doubling length doubles the resistance.

questions.question: Why is the equivalent resistance of a parallel circuit always LESS than the smallest individual resistance in that circuit?
options: Connecting branches in parallel adds more independent pathways for current to flow, increasing total conductance
Current cancels out between opposite branches
Parallel connections cool down the resistors
Voltages subtract from one another across parallel paths
questions.correct_answer: Connecting branches in parallel adds more independent pathways for current to flow, increasing total conductance
questions.explanation: Each added parallel branch provides an additional route for charge flow. Because total conductance is G_total = G1 + G2 + ..., equivalent resistance R_p = 1/G_total is smaller than any individual branch resistance.

questions.question: Why is pure copper widely used for connecting wires in homes, while nichrome is used for toaster heating elements?
options: Copper has very low resistivity to minimize energy loss, while nichrome has high resistivity to produce heat
Copper produces heat more rapidly than nichrome
Nichrome melts at low temperatures to serve as a fuse
Copper is an electrical insulator while nichrome is a superconductor
questions.correct_answer: Copper has very low resistivity to minimize energy loss, while nichrome has high resistivity to produce heat
questions.explanation: Connecting wires must conduct electricity with minimum voltage drop and heating (low ρ). Heating elements require high resistivity (high ρ) and high melting point to glow and dissipate heat (P = I²R).

questions.question: What determines the direction of the magnetic force on a positive charge moving through a magnetic field?
options: The right-hand rule for the vector cross product F = q(v × B)
The direction of gravity acting on the charge
questions.correct_answer: The right-hand rule for the vector cross product F = q(v × B)
questions.explanation: The magnetic Lorentz force is given by F = q(v × B), which acts perpendicular to both velocity v and magnetic field B as dictated by the right-hand rule.

questions.question: Why does no magnetic force act on a stationary charged particle in a magnetic field?
options: Magnetic force requires charge motion (F = qvB sin θ; when v = 0, F = 0)
Stationary charges lose their electric field
Magnetic fields repel stationary electrons completely
Magnetic force only acts on neutral neutrons
questions.correct_answer: Magnetic force requires charge motion (F = qvB sin θ; when v = 0, F = 0)
questions.explanation: A static charge produces only an electrostatic field. A magnetic force arises from interaction with magnetic fields, which requires moving charges (current or velocity v > 0).

questions.question: How does Fleming's Right-Hand Rule differ in application from Fleming's Left-Hand Rule?
options: Right-Hand Rule determines induced current direction in generators; Left-Hand Rule determines force direction in motors
Right-Hand Rule is used for DC motors; Left-Hand Rule is used for AC transformers
Right-Hand Rule calculates electrostatic force; Left-Hand Rule calculates resistance
Both rules give identical directions and can be used interchangeably
questions.correct_answer: Right-Hand Rule determines induced current direction in generators; Left-Hand Rule determines force direction in motors
questions.explanation: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule is the Motor Rule (predicts motion/thrust from current and field). Fleming's Right-Hand Rule is the Generator Rule (predicts induced current from motion and field).

questions.question: Why does an electric motor draw a large surge current when first turned on, but less current once running at full speed?
options: At full speed, the rotating armature generates a back-EMF that opposes supply voltage, reducing net current
The armature resistance increases tenfold as it spins
The battery voltage drops to zero at full speed
Friction stops all electron flow after two seconds
questions.correct_answer: At full speed, the rotating armature generates a back-EMF that opposes supply voltage, reducing net current
questions.explanation: As the motor turns, it acts like a generator producing back-EMF (Eb). The net armature current is I = (V - Eb)/R. At startup Eb = 0, so initial current is very high.

questions.question: What is the role of the carbon brushes in an electric DC motor or generator?
options: They maintain a sliding electrical contact with the rotating split rings without tangling wires
They cool the motor by absorbing friction heat
They insulate the rotor from the metallic casing
questions.correct_answer: They maintain a sliding electrical contact with the rotating split rings without tangling wires
questions.explanation: Carbon brushes are stationary conductive blocks that press gently against rotating commutator segments, completing the circuit while allowing free rotation.

questions.question: What happens when a bar magnet is pushed rapidly into a stationary copper coil connected to a galvanometer?
options: A momentary current is induced in the coil, deflecting the galvanometer pointer
The coil permanently demagnetizes the bar magnet
The copper wire melts due to electrostatic charges
The galvanometer pointer remains strictly at zero
questions.correct_answer: A momentary current is induced in the coil, deflecting the galvanometer pointer
questions.explanation: By Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, moving the magnet changes the magnetic flux through the coil turns, inducing a transient EMF and electric current.

questions.question: Why does a step-up transformer NOT violate the law of conservation of energy when it steps up voltage?
options: The secondary current decreases proportionally, keeping total output power equal to (or slightly less than) input power
Energy is created from magnetic flux inside the iron core
Voltage is not related to electrical energy or power
Transformers only conserve electric charge, not electrical energy
questions.correct_answer: The secondary current decreases proportionally, keeping total output power equal to (or slightly less than) input power
questions.explanation: In an ideal transformer, power in equals power out: P_p = P_s → V_p × I_p = V_s × I_s. Stepping up voltage means secondary current drops by the exact same ratio.

questions.question: Two point charges of +2 μC and +3 μC are separated by a distance of 0.3 m in air. What is the electrostatic repulsive force between them? (k = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²)
A charge of 12 Coulombs flows through an electric lamp in 4 seconds. What is the current flowing through the lamp?
A 100 Ω resistor is connected across a 220 V line. What electric current passes through the resistor?
How much work is done in moving an electric charge of 5 Coulombs across two points having a potential difference of 12 Volts?
questions.explanation: Work done W = Q × V = 5 C × 12 V = 60 Joules.

questions.question: Three resistors of 4 Ω, 6 Ω, and 12 Ω are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
Three resistors of 5 Ω, 10 Ω, and 15 Ω are connected in series across a 60 V battery. What is the current flowing in the circuit?
questions.explanation: Total resistance R_s = 5 + 10 + 15 = 30 Ω. Circuit current I = V / R_s = 60 V ÷ 30 Ω = 2 A.

questions.question: An electric iron rated at 1000 W operates on a 220 V domestic mains supply. What is the current drawn by the iron?
An electric bulb is rated 220 V, 60 W. What is its operating resistance when lit?
A 2000 W electric water geyser is operated for 2 hours every day. How many kilowatt-hours (units) of electrical energy does it consume in a 30-day month?
questions.explanation: Daily energy = 2 kW × 2 h = 4 kWh. Monthly energy = 4 kWh/day × 30 days = 120 kWh.

questions.question: If electricity costs 8 Taka per unit (kWh), what is the monthly cost of operating four 100 W fans running 10 hours daily for 30 days?
questions.explanation: Total power = 4 × 100 W = 400 W = 0.4 kW. Daily energy = 0.4 kW × 10 h = 4 kWh. Monthly units = 4 × 30 = 120 units. Total cost = 120 × 8 = 960 Taka.

questions.question: A straight wire of length 0.5 m carries a current of 4 A perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 Tesla. What is the magnetic force acting on the wire?
A transformer has 500 turns on its primary coil and 2500 turns on its secondary coil. If the primary is connected to a 220 V AC supply, what is the secondary output voltage?
A step-down transformer converts 2200 V down to 220 V. If the secondary coil has 50 turns, how many turns are on the primary coil?
A copper wire has a length of 2 m and a cross-sectional area of 1.7 × 10⁻⁶ m². If the resistivity of copper is 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m, what is its resistance?
A parallel plate capacitor holds a charge of 40 μC when connected across a 20 V battery. What is its capacitance?
questions.explanation: C = Q / V = 40 μC ÷ 20 V = 2 μF.

questions.question: How much energy is stored in a 10 μF capacitor charged to a potential difference of 100 V?
A wire of resistance 16 Ω is cut into four equal pieces, and the four pieces are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance of this combination?
questions.explanation: Cutting into four equal pieces gives each piece a resistance of 16 / 4 = 4 Ω. Connecting four 4 Ω resistors in parallel gives R_p = 4 / 4 = 1 Ω.

questions.question: Two charges of +4 C and -4 C are separated by 2 meters in vacuum. What is the electric field intensity at the exact midpoint between them? (k = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²)
questions.explanation: At midpoint r = 1 m. E from +4 C points toward negative charge: E+ = kq/r² = 9×10⁹×4/1² = 3.6×10¹⁰ N/C. E from -4 C also points toward negative charge: E- = 3.6×10¹⁰ N/C. Net E = E+ + E- = 7.2 × 10¹⁰ N/C.

questions.question: A cell of EMF 6.0 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is connected to an external resistor of 5.5 Ω. What is the terminal potential difference across the cell?
questions.explanation: Current I = E / (R + r) = 6.0 / (5.5 + 0.5) = 1.0 A. Terminal voltage V = E - Ir = 6.0 - (1.0 × 0.5) = 5.5 V.

questions.question: A battery delivers 5 A through an electric toaster for 3 minutes. How much electric charge passes through the toaster in this time?
questions.explanation: t = 3 minutes = 180 seconds. Charge Q = I × t = 5 A × 180 s = 900 Coulombs.

questions.question: In a laboratory, a 50 Ω galvanometer gives full-scale deflection with 2 mA. What shunt resistance must be placed in parallel to convert it into an ammeter reading up to 5 A?
An electric immersion rod of resistance 44 Ω is immersed in water and connected to a 220 V line for 5 minutes. How much heat energy in Joules is generated?
A 100% efficient transformer has a primary coil drawing 2 A at 220 V. If the secondary voltage is 44 V, what is the secondary current?
A uniform wire of resistance R is stretched to double its original length without altering its volume. What is its new resistance?
questions.explanation: Volume V = A × L is constant. When length doubles (L' = 2L), cross-sectional area halves (A' = A/2). New resistance R' = ρ(2L)/(A/2) = 4(ρL/A) = 4R.

questions.question: Two point charges of +1 C and +9 C are fixed 4 m apart. At what distance from the +1 C charge along the line joining them is the net electric field zero?
questions.explanation: kq1/x² = kq2/(d - x)² → 1/x² = 9/(4 - x)² → taking square root: 1/x = 3/(4 - x) → 4 - x = 3x → 4x = 4 → x = 1.0 m.

questions.question: A current of 2 A passes through a solenoid having 500 turns. If the length of the solenoid is 0.5 m, what is the magnetic flux density inside it? (μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A)
A house has five 40 W fluorescent lamps and two 100 W computers running simultaneously. What is the total current drawn from the 220 V supply?
What fuse rating should be selected to protect a circuit powering a 2 kW electric room heater connected to a 220 V mains line?
questions.explanation: Operating current I = P / V = 2000 W ÷ 220 V ≈ 9.09 A. A 10 A fuse is the standard standard commercial rating just above operating current.

questions.question: A charged cloud at a potential of 4 × 10⁷ V discharges 20 C of electric charge to the earth via a lightning flash in 0.001 s. What average electrical power is released during the strike?
questions.explanation: Energy released E = Q × V = 20 C × (4 × 10⁷ V) = 8 × 10⁸ J. Power P = E / t = (8 × 10⁸ J) / (10⁻³ s) = 8 × 10¹¹ W (800 GW).

questions.question: Two resistors of 10 Ω and 20 Ω are connected in series to a 30 V supply. What is the potential difference across the 20 Ω resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance R = 10 + 20 = 30 Ω. Current I = 30 V / 30 Ω = 1 A. Voltage across 20 Ω is V2 = I × R2 = 1 A × 20 Ω = 20 V.

questions.question: An alpha particle (charge +3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) enters a magnetic field of 0.5 T perpendicular to its direction of motion at a speed of 2 × 10⁶ m/s. What is the magnetic force acting on it?
A step-down transformer has an efficiency of 90%. If the input power to the primary coil is 1000 W, what is the output power available at the secondary coil?
questions.explanation: Output power = Efficiency × Input power = 0.90 × 1000 W = 900 W.

questions.question: A 12 V car battery has an internal resistance of 0.04 Ω. When the starter motor draws 150 A, what is the terminal voltage of the battery?
questions.explanation: Internal voltage drop Ir = 150 A × 0.04 Ω = 6.0 V. Terminal voltage V = E - Ir = 12.0 - 6.0 = 6.0 V.

questions.question: In an experiment, the potential difference across a conductor is increased from 10 V to 20 V while its temperature remains constant. What happens to the current flowing through it?
questions.explanation: According to Ohm's law (V = IR), if resistance R is constant, current I is directly proportional to voltage V. Doubling voltage doubles the current.

questions.question: A circuit contains two resistors in parallel: 3 Ω and 6 Ω. What is the power dissipated in the 3 Ω resistor when the pair is connected across a 6 V battery?
questions.explanation: In parallel, each branch experiences the full 6 V. Power in 3 Ω resistor = V² / R = 6² / 3 = 36 / 3 = 12 W.

questions.question: A square loop of wire with an area of 0.04 m² is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the field drops to zero in 0.02 s, what average EMF is induced in the loop?
questions.explanation: Initial flux Φ = B × A = 0.5 × 0.04 = 0.02 Wb. Change in flux ΔΦ = 0.02 Wb. Induced EMF = ΔΦ / Δt = 0.02 Wb / 0.02 s = 1.0 V.

questions.question: A transmission line of resistance 5 Ω carries 20 A of electric current. How much power is dissipated as heat in this transmission line?
